newsitem.title: USA: CIA chief says N.Korea future clear within 3 years.
newsitem.headline: CIA chief says N.Korea future clear within 3 years.

text.p: U.S. CIA Director John Deutch predicted on Wednesday that within three years North Korea would be at war with South Korea, collapse as a state or be on the road to reunification.
"How that proceeds between those three directions will be resolved in the next two or three years. It is not something that will go on for decades," he said, adding this was his own best guess.
Deutch told the Senate Intelligence Committee that he considered it "uncertain" which way communist-ruled North Korea would go.

"Either it's going to...invade the South over one issue or another -- war will break out. Or it will collapse internally or implode because of the incredible economic problems that the country faces. Or, third, it will over time lead to some peaceful resolution and reunification with the South," he testified.

Deutch's appearance before the committee was one of his last acts as U.S. spymaster. President Bill Clinton has nominated his national security adviser, Anthony Lake, to take over the top job at the Central Intelligence Agency.
